primary_onset.model: stratified Cox, threshold-defined first downstream-migration crossing

secondary_terminal_endpoint_membership.source_positive_set_definition: project-specific terminal station/distance rules in upstream identify_escapement_success.R
secondary_terminal_endpoint_membership.boundary: The source meta-analysis explicitly did not analyse escapement success rate because non-membership in the terminal positive set can reflect fishing, detection loss, release geometry and other assumptions. Therefore the complement is not treated as validated biological failure.

secondary_phase_or_ratio_sensitivity.boundary: Retained as a sensitivity contrast only because phase 2 uses terminal positive-set membership whose complement is not a validated failure endpoint.

contextual_external_evidence.source_meta_analysis: Migration speed differs by tidal/non-tidal habitat and WRS context; local hydrology is water-body specific.
contextual_external_evidence.dutch_confirmation_target: Within-route pump -> tidal-sluice study for barrier/opportunity effects after activation.

primary_claim: Capture-time Durif readiness strongly predicts whether and when behavioral migration activates, while the same stage gradient is absent from the source-defined post-activation migration-speed response.
not_claimed: non-membership in successful_migrants_final_detection.csv is biological migration failure
escapement probability is estimated from this reanalysis
external context wholly replaces internal control after activation
Durif stage has exactly zero post-activation effect
the two-phase concept itself is novel
interpretation_priority: activation OR and onset HR are primary internal-state results
post-activation speed is the primary progression result
terminal endpoint membership and stacked phase OR ratio are secondary sensitivity analyses only
next_confirmation: Within-route Dutch pump-to-tidal-sluice data: test barrier/opportunity effects on progression among activated eels without recoding unobserved terminal outcomes as failure.
